idea.body: A matrix is a grid of numbers, and it comes with its own arithmetic. Add or subtract two matrices the same size by combining matching entries. Multiply a matrix by a number by scaling every entry. Multiplying two matrices together works differently. Each entry of the product is a row of the first matrix times a column of the second, added up. A 2 by 2 matrix [a b; c d] has a determinant, a times d minus b times c. That number says whether the matrix has an inverse. When the determinant is not zero, the inverse undoes the matrix. Multiplying both sides of a system by that inverse then solves for every variable at once.

figure.alt: A 2 by 2 matrix drawn as four boxes in a grid: 2, 1 on top, 4, 3 below.

workedExample.prompt:
A = [3 1; 2 1].
Solve 3x + y = 7 and 2x + y = 5 using the inverse of A. What is x?
steps: So x = 2 (and y = 1, from the second row of the same multiplication).

figure.alt: The matrix A, 3 and 1 on top, 2 and 1 below.

ways.name: Add or subtract matrices entry by entry
ways.when: Use this when combining two matrices of the same size.
steps: A + B adds each entry of B to the matching entry of A.
ways.trap: Adding all entries together instead of adding entries in the same position.

figure.alt: Matrix A and matrix B added entry by entry to give the result matrix [3 4; 6 2].

frames.caption: A + B adds matching entries together.

ways.name: Multiply a matrix by a number
ways.when: Use this to scale every entry of a matrix by the same factor.
steps: A = [2 1; 4 3] multiplied by 3 scales every entry.
ways.example: A = [2 1; 4 3]. What is entry (2,2) of 2 times A?
ways.trap: Only multiplying one entry instead of all of them.

ways.name: Multiply two matrices using rows and columns
ways.when: Use this when multiplying a matrix by a vector or two matrices together.
steps: A row times a column means multiply matching entries and add.
Row 1 of A is [1 2]. Column 1 of v is [5; 6].
1 times 5 plus 2 times 6 equals 17 for entry (1,1).
ways.example: A = [1 2; 3 4]. v = [5; 6]. What is entry (2,1) of A times v?
ways.trap: Adding the row and column instead of multiplying matching entries and summing.

ways.name: Find the determinant and check for an inverse
ways.when: Use this to decide if a 2 by 2 matrix has an inverse.
steps: For matrix [a b; c d], the determinant is a times d minus b times c.
If the determinant is not zero, the matrix has an inverse.
If the determinant is zero, the matrix has no inverse.
ways.trap: Computing the determinant as a times b plus c times d, which is the trace instead.

bank.prompt:
A = [2 1; 1 1].
What is entry (1, 1) of the inverse of A?
explanation: The determinant of A is 2(1) - 1(1) = 1.
The inverse of [a b; c d] is 1/det times [d -b; -c a].
So entry (1, 1) of the inverse is 1.
bank.useAgain: when finding the inverse of a 2 by 2 matrix.
hints: Find the determinant first.
The inverse swaps the diagonal entries and negates the other two, then divides by the determinant.
bank.socraticHint: What is the determinant of A, and is it 1 or -1 here?
